name: Green Asia Impex
subscription: 0.03x overall (QIB 0.00x, NII 0.01x, Individual 0.07x) as of 25 Sep 2026, 18:54
lm_rationale: Indorient Financial Services — 2 SME IPOs in 2026 (₹176.69 Cr), 50% positive listings, −11.57% avg listing-day gain (chittorgarh 2026 SME tracker).
net_proceeds: ₹40.03 Cr of net proceeds goes to plant and machinery for a new seafood processing facility (total cost ₹51.27 Cr, ₹10.00 Cr from internal accruals, ₹1.24 Cr already spent), the rest to general corporate purposes; ₹6.96 Cr OFS goes to the promoters.
key_risks: Debt is 2.40x equity (₹99.47 Cr borrowings), operating cash flow was negative in all three years (FY26 −₹6.27 Cr), and China took 31.29% of FY26 revenue.
market_moat: An integrated shrimp processing and export operation in Andhra Pradesh with a 10,800 MTPA facility, selling Vannamei, Black Tiger and freshwater shrimp domestically and to China, the US, UK and Middle East.
management: Promoters Pasupuleti Venkata Ramarao and Pasupuleti Meenakshi; 94.65% pre-issue promoter holding drops to 64.91% post-issue.
prose_business: Green Asia Impex processes and sells frozen shrimp (Vannamei, Black Tiger and freshwater, in HOSO, HLSO and peeled formats) from Eluru district, Andhra Pradesh, and trades dried red chillies. Shrimp made up 87.76% of FY26 revenue from operations, of which domestic sales were 54.25% of the total and exports 33.51%. Chillies contributed 9.77%.
highlight_dev: A new seafood processing facility adds 11,100 MTPA to the existing 10,800 MTPA (total 21,900 MTPA), including IQF, semi-cooked and ready-to-eat shrimp lines.
sector_outlook: The RHP's Ken Research report sizes India's shrimp market at about ₹82,000 crore in FY25, forecast to reach about ₹1,28,400 crore by FY30.
peer_sentence: At 12.31x post-issue FY26 earnings, Green Asia is below the RHP peer average of 16.92x: Apex Frozen Foods 29.16x, Kings Infra Ventures 17.21x and Essex Marine 4.40x.
verdict_reason: 12.31x P/E below 16.92x peer average, but D/E 2.40 and 0.03x Day-2 demand
why: Revenue grew 14.42% to ₹388.63 Cr in FY26 and PAT rose 50.80% to ₹15.61 Cr, though margins are thin at 4.02%. At ₹90 the issue is priced at 12.31x post-issue earnings and 3.21x book, cheaper than the 16.92x RHP peer average. Most of the fresh money funds a capacity-doubling processing plant rather than debt repayment. The balance sheet is the problem: borrowings of ₹99.47 Cr (2.40x equity), negative operating cash flow for three years and 31.29% revenue from China. Indorient's 2026 SME listings average −11.57%, and the book was only 0.03x covered after Day 2.
suggestion: Watch the final-day subscription; apply only if QIB and NII demand picks up, since leverage and the lead manager's record make listing gains uncertain.
